the_bounded_change: The rule-following-partner assumption was replaced by EmpiricalOpponentModel: Laplace-smoothed frequencies of each other agent's observed contributions, updated only from public history, used for expected partner contribution by exact convolution. The hidden-cost belief, planner, environment, utilities, prior, action set and integration gate were all left unchanged. No forced exploration was added: the contributions that appear are expected-value maximisation under the Laplace prior.

failure_rule_applied.not_done: No further SCK feature work, no option B, no MCTS, no nested theory of mind, no new custom benchmark, and no StoryBox or risk-list reconnection.

why_the_repair_only_partly_worked.mechanism: The repair did fix the diagnosed modelling error, and that was worth 57.33 in social utility. But the deeper obstacle is structural: with threshold 6 and a maximum contribution of 3, no single agent can make the project succeed, so universal defection is a Nash equilibrium. A model that learns only from observed contributions has no reason to believe partners will contribute once it has seen them not contribute, so it drifts into the equilibrium it observes. Escaping would require either exploration or a commitment mechanism, both of which peer decision 0023 explicitly excluded from this round.
why_the_repair_only_partly_worked.belief_planning_regression_is_informativ: belief_planning got worse, not better: 0.00 with a zero share of 1.000. Its pledge-conditioning assumes each agent honours a pledge with its measured reliability, and in the all-zero equilibrium every pledge is 0, so the model becomes even more pessimistic than the pure empirical one and locks in immediately. A credible-commitment channel that only mirrors equilibrium pledges actively harms the agent.
why_the_repair_only_partly_worked.consequence: This is the fourth independent negative result for the v0 cognition layer and the first one where the substrate was designed to let it succeed and the diagnosed defect was actually fixed.

honest_notes: The prediction was registered in git before implementation precisely so this scorecard could not be written after the fact to fit the result. One of seven predictions was falsified and is reported as such.

The type-inference Brier for belief (0.558) is worse than for belief_planning (0.357) even though belief_planning learned nothing, because a do-nothing policy keeps near-prior marginals while an active one takes risks. That metric should not be read as belief_planning being better calibrated; the believed-versus-realised success columns are the interpretable calibration signal.

This is an own-authored substrate and 30 episodes, so it is smoke evidence. It was accepted by the peer as sufficient for the go or no-go decision this round was defined to make, and the fixed-rule comparison does not depend on fine margins: 72.80 against 57.33 with the efficiency gap 0.554 against 0.394.
recommended_next_engineering_priority: Return to StoryBox and novel work as peer decision 0023 directs. The two negative benchmarks and the retained interfaces are the durable output of this line; they should be cited as negative evidence rather than re-litigated without a new explicit decision.
